From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 13:28:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Dedicated capacity need — internal sizing notes

Kim / Priyom —

I ran the numbers from Chris's traffic snapshot and sketched two committed capacity options. Assumptions up front:
- Baseline model: open-7B variant (FP16) for short chat-turns; long-gen uses an opt-tuned 13B variant.
- Perf numbers (empirical on our fleet):
  • open-7B FP16: ~750 tokens/sec per A100-80GB equivalent (dedicated inference runtime, steady-state with batching).
  • open-7B int8 (QAT-like profile): ~1,350 tokens/sec per A100-80GB eq. (quantization gains when sequences are short).
  • 13B opt: ~220 tokens/sec per A100 (FP16), or ~380 tokens/sec per A100 (int8-ish).
- Effective mix: 90% short-turns (7B), 10% long-gen (13B).

Option A — Conservative commit (minimize ops complexity):
- Provision for sustained daytime 1.8k tokens/sec + 2x cushion for short bursts -> target sustained capacity = 3.6k tokens/sec.
- Map to GPUs (FP16 plan): 3 x A100 (3 * 750 = 2,250 tokens/sec) — still shy of 3.6k; so recommend 5 x A100 to meet cushion (5 * 750 = 3,750).
- Long-gen: separate pool of 1 x A100 (220 tokens/sec) + queued preemption rules; rely on burst routing.
- Pros: conservative latency headroom, simpler model parity with hosted variants.
- Cons: higher unit cost.

Option B — Quantized/efficiency-first commit (preferred cost/core tradeoff):
- Use int8-ish quant profiles for 7B where accuracy tests pass. Effective per-GPU 1,350 tps.
- For daytime sustained 1.8k baseline + expected hourly bursts (12k peaks):
  • Baseline cushion target = baseline * 2 = 3.6k -> needs 3 x A100 (3 * 1,350 = 4,050).
  • Burst handling: 12k tokens/sec peak for 3 minutes once/hour -> we recommend burst pool of 4 x A100 (quant profile) pre-warmed and a prioritized routing policy that shifts long-gen to overflow nodes. Burst pool provides ~5,400 tps — still below 12k, so pair with temporary cross-region fallback to hosted pool (or dedicated ephemeral burst GPUs).
- Long-gen (13B): quant gains smaller — recommend 2 x A100 with int8 pipeline for background jobs (2 * 380 = 760 tps).
- Pros: ~35–45% cost reduction vs Option A for steady-state.
- Cons: requires validation of quant profile; more complex rollout and gating.

SLO fit (p95 latency <= 250ms for short-turns):
- With Option A (FP16, 5 GPUs) we estimate p95 ~190–230ms under sustained load (with KV cache warm).
- With Option B (quantized, 3 GPUs + burst) we estimate p95 ~210–260ms: good for baseline but risk during unmodeled sustained bursts; hence the need for cross-pool fallback.

Recommended next steps:
1) Run a small quantization validation test on 10k production-sampled short-turns (accuracy & hallucination checks).
2) If pass, proceed with Option B + ephemeral burst plan (3 committed GPUs + 4 burst GPUs) and contractual language for ephemeral burst support.
3) Priyom to draft rollout runbook (canary, A/B latency verification, fallback to hosted). Rishi to size KV cache memory and pre-warm plan.

Attaching a short pdf with the perf assumptions (quant_profiles_summary.pdf).

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing — recommendation and next steps

Chris —

Thanks for the quick data. Based on Ben's modeling, our proposal for the Fathom dedicated commit is below. High level: two-phase commit that balances cost and latency risk.

Phase 1 (initial commit, ~Q3 start):
- Committed: 3 x A100-80GB (quant profile for 7B) + 2 x A100 for 13B background jobs.
- Burst strategy: ephemeral burst pool (4 x A100 pre-warmed on demand) + contractual hosted fallback for extreme unplanned peaks.
- Expected steady-state cost reduction vs FP16 plan: ~40% (subject to quant validation).
- p95 short-turn latency target (post-canary): <= 250ms.

Phase 2 (post-validation + scale):
- Move to full quantized steady fleet if accuracy/QA passes; increase committed burst slab to handle longer >10-minute spikes if observed.

Action items:
- Fathom: provide 10k short-turn samples for quant validation and confirm any function/tool-call frequency (Chris).
- Redwood: Priyom to produce rollout runbook and canary checklist (target 2-week canary). Ben to run a latency-stress sim in staging (3 days).
- Legal/Proc: if you want the ephemeral burst guarantee in the contract, loop your procurement/legal and we can surface SOW language.

If that looks good I'll prepare a formal MA/commit sheet with pricing and an ops handoff.

Best,
Kimberly Park
